findings.rationale: The Skeleton King is explaining why Jin is angry at Yamamoto, not accusing Jin of using the slur.
findings.replacement: “Because the monkey human called the wicked human *Chōsenjin*.”

findings.current: “You really want me to hit you?”
findings.defect: Makes Choi the threatened target instead of Yamamoto.
findings.rationale: Jin is checking that Choi will let him strike Yamamoto once.
findings.replacement: “I’m really going to hit him, you know?”

findings.current: “I heard the reinforcements arriving, so I left.”
findings.defect: Changes the person who left the scene from the Prophet to Yamamoto.
findings.rationale: Choi has just asked why the Prophet left an S-rank Hunter alive.
findings.replacement: “He heard the reinforcements arriving and left.”
findings.source: “지원 병력이 도착하는 소리를 듣고 자리를 떠났습니다.”

findings.current:
That was why even satellites in orbit couldn’t detect them, despite coming within a few kilometers.

No—even if the satellites came right overhead, it would be the same.
findings.defect: Assigns the ground-level approach to the satellites rather than the approaching people.
findings.rationale: The passage distinguishes satellite surveillance from people approaching the concealed group at ground level.
findings.replacement:
That was why even satellites in orbit couldn’t detect them—and why the infidels couldn’t find them despite drawing within a few kilometers.

No, the infidels wouldn’t find them even if they came right up to them.
findings.source:
우주에 떠 있는 인공위성으로도, 불과 수 킬로미터 남짓한 거리까지 다가왔음에도 그들을 발견할 수 없는 이유는 그 때문이다.

아니, 설령 코앞까지 다가온다 해도 마찬가지다.

findings.current: Yamamoto Genji was now bowing as politely as he possibly could.
findings.defect: Adds a bow before Yamamoto’s subsequent, distinctly described dogeza.
findings.rationale: The source describes his manner here, not a physical bow.
findings.replacement: Yamamoto Genji had become the picture of politeness.
findings.source: 그곳에는 한껏 공손해진 야마모토 겐지가 있었다.

findings.current: “As far as I know, it means something similar to the N-word.”
findings.defect: Euphemizes the Skeleton King’s explicit comparison.
findings.rationale: He says the slur outright; replacing it with “the N-word” softens his blunt speech.
findings.replacement: “As far as I know, it means about the same thing as ‘nigger.’”
findings.source: “이 몸이 아는 바에 의하면, 니거랑 비슷한 뜻이다.”

findings.current: Whatever else, he’d come all the way to the Middle East because I’d asked him to.
findings.defect: Turns Jin’s command responsibility into a personal request.
findings.rationale: Jin’s authority over the mission grounds the responsibility he takes in the following lines.
findings.replacement: Whatever else, he’d come all the way to the Middle East on my orders.
findings.source: 어쨌거나 내 뜻에 따라 머나먼 중동까지 온 자다.

findings.current: “You couldn’t hold him back even with two of you.”
findings.defect: Distances the Skeleton King from the proposed two-person effort.
findings.rationale: Choi is asking the Skeleton King to help; the reply dismisses what they could accomplish together.
findings.replacement: “Even the two of us couldn’t stop him.”

findings.current: “……Did you go to some kind of dojo for groveling?”
findings.defect: Changes the joke’s imaginary dogeza school into a dojo and replaces the specific practice with generic groveling.
findings.rationale: The source names dogeza and jokes that Yamamoto must have studied it at a school.
findings.replacement: “……Did you go to a dogeza academy or something?”

findings.defect: Capitalizes an ordinary category contrary to the supplied glossary.
findings.rationale: This is the reveal of the Prophet’s nature, not a new proper title.

summary: The draft has several action and subject reversals, plus a softened slur and a few localized wording issues.
